
## Step 2 — Push to GitHub

1. Go to [github.com/new](https://github.com/new) and create a new **private** repo called `unity-dashboard`
2. Then back in your terminal:

```powershell
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/unity-dashboard.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

## Step 3 — Deploy Frontend to Vercel (2 minutes, no CLI needed)

1. Go to [vercel.com](https://vercel.com) → **Add New Project**
2. **Import** your `unity-dashboard` GitHub repo
3. When it asks for the **Root Directory**, type `frontend` ← this is the key step
4. Vercel will auto-detect Next.js — leave the build settings as-is
5. Add this **Environment Variable** before deploying:
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` → your backend's live URL (e.g. `https://unity-api.railway.app`)
6. Click **Deploy** — every future push to `main` auto-deploys

## Step 4 — Deploy Backend to Railway

The backend is an Express + SQL Server app, so it needs its own server. [Railway](https://railway.app) is the easiest free option:

1. Go to [railway.app](https://railway.app) → **New Project** → **Deploy from GitHub repo**
2. Select `unity-dashboard`, set **Root Directory** to `backend`
3. Add your environment variables (from your `.env` file):
   - `DB_SERVER`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_PORT`
   - `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` → your Vercel URL (e.g. `https://unity-dashboard.vercel.app`)
4. Railway gives you a public URL — copy it back into Vercel as `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`

---

### What I've already set up for you

- **`.gitignore`** — covers `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `.env`, `.env.local`, logs, etc. so secrets never get committed
- **`frontend/vercel.json`** — tells Vercel exactly how to build the Next.js app

Once both are deployed, the full flow is: **push to GitHub `main` → Vercel auto-builds frontend + Railway auto-redeploys backend**. Your team just needs the Vercel URL to access it.
